codeReview.summary: The feature removed empty catch blocks from production TypeScript code and correctly added logging or documented intentional no-op handling in the targeted extension files, but it does not satisfy the stated expected behavior because empty catch blocks remain in the repository under tests.

issues.description: An empty `catch {}` remains when removing the temporary user data directory. The feature expectedBehavior says no empty catch blocks remain in the codebase, and the handoff also claims `grep -r 'catch\s*{\s*}' packages/ --include='*.ts'` found none. Repository review still finds empty catches in test code, so the implementation does not fully satisfy VAL-CRIT-004 as written.
An empty polling-loop `catch {}` remains around relay readiness checks, contradicting the feature requirement that all empty catch blocks be handled.
An empty cleanup `catch {}` remains around `child.kill('SIGTERM')`, so the repo still contains unhandled empty catches after this feature.
An empty relay readiness polling `catch {}` remains in test code, so the codebase-wide assertion is not met.
An empty `catch {}` remains around `document.getAnimations?.()` access in the perf harness. This leaves the repository with unresolved empty catches despite the feature claiming all were fixed.
An empty cleanup `catch {}` remains around removing the temp user data directory, so the repository still violates the no-empty-catch expectation.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The cleanup-worker skill instructs workers to search broadly for empty catches, but its verification language does not explicitly call out whether tests must be included. The worker interpreted the scope as `packages/` only in the final verification, which let test-file empty catches slip through even though the feature metadata says `No empty catch {} blocks remain in codebase`.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: cleanup-worker SKILL.md says `Find empty catches` with a repo-wide grep example and `Verification: No empty catch blocks remain`; handoff verification instead used `grep -r 'catch\s*{\s*}' packages/ --include='*.ts'`, and repo review still finds six matches under `tests/`.

summary: Fail: production targets were updated appropriately, including the requested extension files, but six empty `catch {}` blocks remain in test TypeScript files, so the codebase-wide requirement was not actually met.
